gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-bengali: Styro is retro and a little bossy, its letters jammed shoulder to shoulder. Noto Sans Bengali loosens everything up beside it, with open mouths and capitals barely above the lowercase, a plain sans that lets the heading do the shouting.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-bhaiksuki: Commanding and tightly packed, Styro crowds its letters until the curves nearly shut. Noto Sans Bhaiksuki follows with plump, rope-like lowercase and open apertures, so the page gets a loud start and a friendly, easy landing.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-brahmi: Styro looks retro and pressed together, with curves that almost close up on themselves. Noto Sans Brahmi sits next to it with a high mean line and curves left open, a plain sans that feels lighter and more current beside such a stout neighbor.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-buginese: Styro packs its sizable lowercase tight, with curves that barely leave a gap. And Noto Sans Buginese does the opposite job, opening its letter mouths like unjoined chalk arcs under short ascenders, which suits sustained text in a way the heading never tries to.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-buhid: Noto Sans Buhid has a high x-height and generous gaps where curves meet the stem. Under Styro's crowded, retro heading, a plain sans like this would let paragraphs run smoothly, with plenty of breathing room between every line.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-carian: Noto Sans Carian reads crisp and spaced out, its terminals parting like open scissor blades. And under Styro's cramped, commanding heading, a plain sans this clear would make long paragraphs feel easy to move through.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-chakma: Approachable and open, with roomy mouths on every s and c. Styro stamps a retro, crowded headline on top, while Noto Sans Chakma brings its lowercase up close to the caps and lets the text breathe below.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-cham: Styro is retro and commanding, with e and c shapes squeezed nearly shut. Noto Sans Cham is all open entries and tall rounded lowercase, a plain sans that would look lost if the heading were made small.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-cherokee: Crowded, retro letters with barely any gap in the e or c give Styro its muscle. But Noto Sans Cherokee sits in a tall band with short stalks and a wide-open e, so a long passage would read smoothly and openly.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-chorasmian: Tight, loud and retro, Styro jams its letters together. Yet Noto Sans Chorasmian stops its curves short with a large x-height and short ascenders, so a long passage in this sans would feel spacious and easy.
